headline: Oregon's governor has ordered state environmental regulators to stop issuing air and water pollution permits for new or expanding data centers until July 2027, which would effectively pause most large data center building in the state.
score_reason: Not stale or overstated: a governor's written order that halts most new data center permits in a major data center state, first made public on 13 Oct 2026.
importance_line: Residents of Oregon's data center towns and state regulators are affected first, then Amazon and other large builders, but the pause rests on a governor's letter rather than a new law, so its enforcement and what follows July 2027 are not yet clear.
summary: OPB reports that Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek told the state's Department of Environmental Quality in a letter to pause pollution permits for new or expanding data centers and to stop processing wastewater permit changes made for them, widening an earlier pause on state-owned land. Amazon, which runs more than a dozen large data centers in eastern Oregon, said it was disappointed and warned of lost jobs and investment, while Kotek and her Republican challenger Christine Drazan both say they favor a moratorium.
